summary.headline: Timken India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 25.4% YoY to INR 969 crore, with PBT up 29.5% to INR 156 crore and PBT margin at 16.1%.
summary.overview: Management reported strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with standalone revenue of INR 969 crore (up 25.4% YoY and about 4.3% QoQ) and PAT of INR 116 crore (up 29.7% YoY). Margins improved despite higher depreciation from new vessels, fuel and gas costs. The new Bharuch plant is ramping up, with SRB lines at 70% utilisation and CRB lines below 60%, and revenue from the plant at about INR 75 crore. Management flagged rising input costs, a delayed rail tender that has since moved toward orders, and an unfavourable mix that drove a 130 bps gross margin decline QoQ.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 786 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR 156.7 crore in Q2, 16% of revenue; low share as the global rail tender was delayed, which drove the unfavourable mix.

segments.name: Process industries
segments.commentary: INR 190.9 crore, 20% of revenue; wind cited as doing well, and management expects stable growth ex-CRB/SRB.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR 262.7 crore, 27% of revenue; up about 60% YoY and 30% QoQ per analyst's figures, with export incentives reported separately.

segments.name: Bharuch (CRB/SRB)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR 75 crore in Q2; plant at about 60% average utilisation, SRB lines at 70% and CRB lines below 60%; sales mainly intercompany exports.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 utilisation at Bharuch expected at about 70-75% overall, with CRB at 50-60% and SRB at 70% as of the call.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR 120 crore): trial runs in November-December 2026, followed by PPAP and qualification; commercial production targeted by December.
Railway tender expected to convert to orders within about 3 weeks, with interim wagon-builder orders already placed.
Management expects overall export momentum to be healthy in coming quarters, with rail exports more gradual.
Cost inflation (carbides, steel, gases, labour) expected to continue; management aims to pass it on to customers.
Q3 seasonality expected to soften because of calendar year-end export timing.
Proposed amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited into Timken India is progressing; regulatory process ongoing.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramp-up: lines capitalised; overall utilisation about 60% in Q2, with SRB at 70% and CRB below 60%.
Jamshedpur rail expansion, about INR 120 crore, on target; trial runs Nov-Dec 2026.
Plain bearing investment at Bharuch on target; GGB FRC and metal polymer investments of about INR 35 crore each (INR 70 crore total), approved and underway, with asset turn of about 1.5-2x.
Management said GGB machines are installed at Bharuch but not yet capitalised; imported GGB product currently sold while local production is pending.
demand_pricing: Demand described as okay across key end markets; domestic demand seen as robust given GDP growth of about 7% and infrastructure spending.
Rail and heavy truck seen as attractive segments; off-highway behaving well globally and in India.
Price pass-through: management said the industry cannot absorb input cost increases and aims to pass them on; automotive customers may delay pass-through.
Gross margin down about 130 bps QoQ: roughly 50% from unfavourable mix (lower rail and distribution share) and 50% from input cost vs price timing.
Wind: domestic wind market recovering; Timken India sells gearbox bearings and buys main-shaft wind bearings from sister concerns.
India cost competitiveness described as favourable versus global peers, though not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise revenue for Q2 and Bharuch utilisation versus the 70% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Segment split given (Rail 16%, Mobile others 21%, Distribution 15%, Process 20%, Exports 27%). Overall Bharuch utilisation about 60%; SRB at 70%, CRB below 60%; Bharuch revenue about INR 75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the cost increase be passed on, and how much did it impact Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry must pass costs on; automotive will delay. The 130 bps gross margin decline was split about 50/50 between unfavourable mix and input cost timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall and CWIP double?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the drop was an accounting reclassification between other expenses and depreciation of about INR 1.3 crore, not a structural decline.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch margins versus TRB, and the Jamshedpur rail timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are not disclosed at plant level; industrial CRB/SRB directionally better than automotive. Rail expansion trial runs in Nov-Dec, with qualification to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bharuch's utilisation reach 80-85% by year-end, and how does the mix affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 70-75% overall by year-end; margin accretion expected once critical mass is reached, with CFO noting Q3 seasonal softening.

qa_highlights.question: How is wind positioned, and is GGB winning orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Timken India focuses on gearbox bearings, not main-shaft; GGB has not yet capitalised local production but is winning orders via imported product, with local output at Bharuch to follow.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (carbides, steel, gas, fuel, labour) with limited ability to absorb; timing gap in price pass-through.
Automotive customers may delay price pass-through.
Bharuch ramp-up pace: CRB lines below 60% utilisation and reliance on intercompany exports for current sales.
Rail tender conversion into orders and rail mix, which drove the QoQ margin drop.
Depreciation step-up from new vessels and Bharuch; CWIP nearly doubled.
Geopolitical and trade uncertainty affecting global demand and supply chains.
Pending amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology into Timken India.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the top-line run-rate, but cautious on cost inflation and the Bharuch ramp, which management said is still below target. Management was candid on the Bharuch utilisation gap and on the timing of rail orders, and it deflected precise margin figures (Bharuch margins, cost-competitiveness) by giving directional answers only.

adds.what: GGB FRC and metal polymer investments at Bharuch (about INR 35 crore each, INR 70 crore total)

growth.why: Management guides Bharuch year-end utilisation to 70-75% and expects the rail tender to convert to orders in about 3 weeks, backed by the Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR 120 crore, trial runs Nov-Dec 2026) and interim wagon orders, though the Q3 seasonal softness and unquantified rail/export timing keep backing partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 130 bps QoQ (half mix, half input-cost timing), but management expects margin accretion once Bharuch reaches critical mass and aims to pass on cost inflation; Q2 EBITDA margin was about 19.2%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR 120 crore) is on target with trial runs in Nov-Dec 2026 and commercial production targeted by December; Bharuch lines are already capitalised and ramping at about 60% utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 25.4% YoY to INR 969 crore in Q2, exports were up about 60% YoY, and Bharuch utilisation is guided to 70-75% by FY27 year-end from about 60% now.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 60% at Bharuch, so no new capacity is needed soon; the INR 70 crore GGB FRC and metal polymer investments are already approved and underway, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew about 20% in H1 FY27 and rail orders are expected within about 3 weeks, but cost inflation and a Q3 seasonal softening limit upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost inflation (carbides, steel, gases, labour) is expected to continue, automotive customers may delay price pass-through, and Q3 seasonality is expected to soften, while the Bharuch ramp is still below target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GGB FRC and metal polymer products are under construction at Bharuch (INR 70 crore total) with local production pending, and the imported GGB product is already being sold.

rows.label: Rail tender conversion into orders
rows.why: Management expects the delayed global rail tender to convert to orders in about 3 weeks, with interim wagon-builder orders already placed, which would lift the Rail share (16% of Q2 revenue) and reverse the mix drag.

rows.label: Amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology into Timken India
rows.why: The proposed amalgamation is progressing but the regulatory process is still ongoing, so timing is not fixed.

rows.label: Pass-through of input cost inflation
rows.why: Management says the industry cannot absorb carbide, steel and gas inflation and aims to pass it on, but automotive customers may delay, and the 130 bps QoQ gross margin hit was about half input-cost timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand and the top-line run-rate (revenue +25.4% YoY) but cautious on cost inflation and the Bharuch ramp, which is about 60% against a 70% target; analysts pressed on Bharuch utilisation, margin mix, and the depreciation and CWIP movements.
